=========================

Once you understand the business and have established an operating plan with the founders, you will have authority to allocate the approved budget, make hiring and firing decisions, change leadership when needed, and direct marketing execution. We expect you to use that authority and develop leaders who own their responsibilities.  
You will work with the founders on firm strategy and major investments, keeping us informed about performance and significant decisions. We welcome thoughtful challenge, clear recommendations, and sound judgment. Attorneys retain responsibility for legal judgment and litigation strategy.  
  
**What you will own**

**Priorities and execution**
============================

Translate the partners’ vision into the annual plan and quarterly Rocks. Bring your recommendation on what matters most, identify capacity constraints, and keep the firm focused—including telling the founders when we are adding too much.  
Run leadership meetings that end in decisions, owners, and deadlines. Make sure the work gets done between meetings and that department leaders take responsibility for results.

**Business reporting and analytics**
====================================

Complete the reporting buildout with Finance and Technology: consistent KPI definitions, reliable data, named owners, and dashboards leaders actually use. Determine the expertise needed, whether an analyst hire or outside support, and drive the work to completion. This is a core first-year deliverable.  
Understand the numbers well enough to challenge assumptions, explain what is changing, and recommend action. Connect marketing, intake, case inventory, staffing, and financial information.

**Marketing and intake**
========================

Own case acquisition economics end to end: spend, lead quality, conversion, cost per qualified signed case, and expected case value by market, practice area, and channel. Hold Marketing and Intake leaders accountable for both case quality and signed-case targets.  
Pressure-test changes in spending and strategy. Watch leading indicators and act before a shortfall becomes a revenue problem, accounting for different PI and mass tort timelines. Assess whether the right people are in the right seats and make changes when needed.

**Financial visibility**
========================

Partner with Finance on the operating budget, compensation and staffing models, forecasting, and monthly variance reviews. Resolve variances with the responsible department leaders.  
Maintain a rolling view of cash and case inventory that connects expected fee timing to spending and hiring decisions. Make assumptions and uncertainty visible, and distinguish operating performance from the timing of individual case recoveries.

**Client experience and innovation**
====================================

Take ownership of implementing our client journey vision. Set priorities, assign owners, and turn ideas into measurable improvements from intake through resolution. Work with legal leaders to remove operational barriers to case progress, settlement, and trial readiness.  
Evaluate technology, AI, and process changes through focused pilots. Measure whether they improve client service or team effectiveness, protect confidential information, and ensure successful changes become part of everyday work.

**Leadership and people**
=========================

Lead department heads, address missed commitments directly, and develop managers who solve problems at their own level. Partner with People Services on hiring, onboarding, development, and performance management.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
Our client runs the compliant system of record you build on to move, store, and grow money. Launch financial products your customers love. We provide the financial primitives, licenses, and compliance, and our forward deployed team gets you live in two weeks. Under the hood, fiat and blockchain run as one system. Their customers never see any of it. Money comes in, money goes out, and it just gets there.

**The Role**

Our customers don't just call our APIs. They build their products on us. Their balances, their payment operations, their compliance state. Which means our business succeeds exactly as far as theirs do. Forward Deployed Engineering is the team that makes that true, one customer at a time.

You'll report to our CTO and embed with one strategic customer at a time, the enterprises building their products where we're investing deepest. You'll understand their business, their constraints, and their pain points better than anyone, and then you'll build what their launch needs.

Here's a concrete example. A global payouts customer is expanding into a new market where we don't yet have local account infrastructure. You scope the requirements with their engineering team, then build the virtual account infrastructure, in our core codebase, that their launch depends on. When it ships, it's not a one-off. It becomes a core product that we sell to the next ten customers.

That's the defining property of this role. This is not a services role, and it's not technical support. You're a product engineer whose roadmap comes from a live customer instead of a planning doc. Everything you build lands in the core platform, and the best of it becomes product the whole company resells. Engagements are scoped at contract time. You're delivering what we've committed to, not absorbing unbounded requests. But within that scope, the what, the why, and the how are yours to figure out with the customer.

**What You'll Do**

* **Deploy into customer contexts.** Iterate daily with your customer's engineering and operations teams, mostly over Zoom and Slack, with some travel to spend real time on site.
* **Scope the build with the customer.** You're not handed a spec. You work out what to build and why with the customer directly, paired with a deployment strategist who owns the commercial side.
* **Build across the full stack.** TypeScript and React, NestJS with Postgres and Prisma, and AWS (SQS, SNS, Lambda). New account infrastructure, blockchain integrations, API endpoints, compliance workflows, whatever the launch requires.
* **Generalize the bespoke.** Identify patterns across implementations and work with product to turn engagement output into first-class platform features.
* **Prototype fast, ship carefully.** Rapid iteration against live customer workflows, accepting some throwaway work and making sure what isn't throwaway gets productized properly, all while debugging production issues in real time, sometimes with the customer watching.
* **Design for correctness and auditability.** This is money-movement infrastructure. Edge cases have real consequences, and you think about failure modes before they happen.
* **Communicate crisply** with customer engineers, operators, founders, and finance leaders, and with our own product leads, whose pods your work must generalize into.

**Who You Are**

* **You're a builder first.** We're flexible on tenure. We'll hire a scrappy engineer straight out of school or a seasoned customer-facing engineer. We're not flexible on the bar. You ship production-grade, full-stack work, and you have something you've built to prove it.
* **You're AI-native.** Agentic tools are how you already build, and we'll ask you to show us.
* **You're energized by customers, not shielded from them.** You're comfortable operating directly with an enterprise engineering team, under ambiguity, where the requirements are yours to discover.
* **You're obsessed with correctness and resilience.** You love a good state machine. You think carefully about what happens when things go wrong, because with money they can't.
* **Strong pluses.** Payments and fintech infrastructure experience, blockchain and stablecoin integration work, and a forward-deployed or solutions architect background where you *built* rather than just configured.

**What Success Looks Like**

* Your customer launches on time, on our rails, and their volume ramps because what you built works.
* The infrastructure you shipped for one customer is now core product being sold to the next ten.
* Your customer's engineering team treats you as one of their own, and our team trusts what you merge.
* You've defined, alongside our CTO, what "forward deployed" means.
* You're an early member of a function we're building the company around.

**How We Work**

We run on three principles:

* **2% better, every day.** One percent for yourself, one percent for the people around you.
* **Telos.** From the Greek word telos, meaning not just done but fulfilled. Everyone here is focused on one mission and knows each other's Telos.
* **Build.** Embody the builder's mindset. Make things, solve problems, and have fun doing it.

* Experience building real-time risk systems.

Bilt is the membership for where you live.

  
  

What started as a way to reward people on their largest expense has turned into an ecosystem connecting our members, property managers and local merchants.

The Metropolitan Transportation Authority is North America's largest transportation network, serving a population of 15.3 million people across a 5,000-square-mile travel area surrounding New York City, Long Island, southeastern New York State, and Connecticut. The MTA network comprises the nation's largest bus fleet and more subway and commuter rail cars than all other U.S. transit systems combined.

The MTA Rolling Stock Program is responsible for achieving the best value for the MTA's rolling stock acquisitions and ensuring dedicated attention to the acquisition and lifetime costs of these strategic assets. Acquiring and maintaining rolling stock that supports reliable service at the MTA's scale is increasingly data-driven, and the Rolling Stock Program's Strategy & Analysis team is central to that work.

Working closely with operating units and HQ departments, the Senior Director ensures the development of realistic implementation plans for approved initiatives and provides sufficient support and tracking through execution.

**Job Description**

THE SELECTED CANDIDATE WILL BE OFFERED A SALARY BETWEEN $87,743.00 - $100,904.00.
  
  
The Administration for Children’s Services (ACS) protects and promotes the safety and well-being of children and families through child welfare and juvenile justice services and community supports. ACS manages community-based supports and foster care services and provides subsidized childcare vouchers. ACS child protection staff respond to allegations of child maltreatment. In juvenile justice, ACS oversees detention, placement and programs for youth in the community.
  
  
The Division of Child and Family Well-Being (CFWB) works to ensure families and children have the critical supports they need to thrive and exercise self-determination. CFWB leverages concrete resources, stakeholder relationships, and community and family strengths to drive toward greater equity and social justice, reduce disparities and disproportionality - including in the child welfare system -, and create conditions that foster well-being for families and children across New York City. Our work includes the provision of child care assistance; support for caregivers and child-serving professionals to prevent child injury; and investment in community-based approaches.
  
  
The Office of Strategy, Research, and Provider Partnerships (SRPP) in the Division of Child and Family Well Being (CFWB) at ACS consists of four teams that manage ACS’s Family Enrichment Centers and PromiseNYC programs and lead strategic, analytical, and data-driven collaborative portfolios of work to support CFWB offices, programs, and policies. The teams include – FEC Program Management (FEC PM), Child Care Data Management (DM), Strategy and Research (SR), and Program Sustainability and Improvement team (PSI).
  
  
The FEC Program Management team oversees the development and implementation of 30 contracted Family Enrichment Centers citywide, providing budget management, coaching, and technical assistance to contracted staff at each FEC to ensure it is implemented with high quality and alignment with the Model Standards.
  
  
In 2017, The Administration for Children's Services launched three Family Enrichment Centers (FEC). As of January 2026, there are 30 FECs across the five boroughs of New York City, all in varying stages of implementation – some have been open and operating for several years; others are in a start-up phase, working to hire and train staff, engage community members to design and renovate their sites, conduct outreach, and provide in-person and virtual offerings.
  
  
FECs are welcoming walk-in family- centered spaces, open to all, that are co-designed with community members. At the centers, families and children can connect with neighbors, volunteer their time, participate in various offerings, and access resources and supports they feel they need to thrive. In July 2025, our contract with the thirtieth and final FEC will begin.
  
  
The Manager, ACS Family Enrichment Center (FEC) Program Management team oversees an assigned portfolio of contracted Family Enrichment Centers and serves as the primary liaison between ACS and contracted provider organizations. The Manager supports high-quality, community-centered implementation of the FEC model by balancing contract oversight, technical assistance, relationship management, and continuous learning in alignment with the FEC Model Standards and ACS expectations.
  
  
Key Responsibilities:
  
  
1. Contract Oversight & Accountability
  
  

* Manage an assigned portfolio of FEC contracts and serve as the primary ACS point of contact
* Monitor provider alignment with FEC Model Standards, contract requirements, and deliverables through the implementation of the Program Management Team’s data/information collection, analysis, and reporting systems and tools
* Review provider reports, workplans, and corrective action plans; identify risks and implementation gaps
* Document performance concerns and elevate issues to Directors with clear analysis and recommendations
* Review and approval of annual budgets, budget modifications, and invoices through the City’s PASSPort Portal

  
2. FEC Model Implementation & Technical Assistance
  
  

* Provide ongoing coaching and technical assistance to contracted FEC Directors and leadership staff
* Support translation of FEC Model Standards into contracted providers’ daily practice, policies, staffing, and programming
* Conduct regular site visits (announced and unannounced) to assess implementation quality and fidelity

title: Manager, Tax
description:
### **About Mecka AI**

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.  
We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.  
We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

**About the Role**
------------------

Tax touches every part of our business model: the entities and teams we run in several jurisdictions, the payments we send across borders to a large base of contributors and partners, the capture hardware that moves between countries, and the data we license to customers in other markets. As we grow, each of these turns into real filings and liabilities, and the structure behind them has to hold up with auditors, investors, and tax authorities.

As Manager, Tax, you will own direct and indirect tax across every entity and market, run compliance and the income tax provision with our accounting team and outside advisors, and set the transfer pricing that governs how our entities deal with one another. You will also advise our commercial, operations, and legal teams on the tax consequences of new markets, deals, and acquisitions before we commit to them.

**What You Will Do**
--------------------

* Compliance: Own the tax calendar and every filing across our entities, including corporate income tax, sales tax, VAT and GST returns, withholding, and information reporting, whether the work is prepared in-house or by outside advisors.
* Provision and audit: Prepare the income tax provision under US GAAP (ASC 740) with our accounting team, including deferred taxes, valuation allowances, and uncertain tax positions, and own the tax side of every financial statement audit.
* Transfer pricing: Build and maintain the transfer pricing policy, intercompany agreements, and documentation that set how our entities charge one another, and make sure monthly intercompany invoicing follows the policy.
* New markets: Assess the tax footprint of each new country and operating model before we open, covering entity and partner structures, permanent establishment exposure, local registrations, and the tax cost of each option.
* Cross-border payments: Set the tax rules for paying contributors, merchants, and partners in many countries, including withholding, payee tax forms, and reporting, and work with logistics on import duties and taxes on capture hardware.
* Deals and acquisitions: Advise on the tax structure of customer and partner agreements and of acquisitions of companies, datasets, and other assets, so the tax cost of every deal is known and priced before signature.
* Advisors and authorities: Select and manage outside tax advisors across jurisdictions against clear scopes and budgets, respond to notices and audits from tax authorities, and claim the credits and incentives we qualify for, such as research and development credits.

**What You Bring**
------------------

* Experience: 5 to 8+ years in tax, including time at a Big Four or national accounting firm and in-house at a high-growth company operating in several countries.
* Qualification: CPA, CA, or an equivalent accounting or tax qualification.
* International tax: Hands-on experience with corporate income tax, transfer pricing, withholding, and indirect tax across several countries at once, including intercompany arrangements you have built or maintained.
* Provision: You have prepared or reviewed an income tax provision under ASC 740 and taken it through an external audit.
* Business judgment: You turn complex tax rules and advisor memos into clear decisions and next steps for teams outside finance.
* AI fluency: You use AI tools in your day-to-day work to research rules, prepare workpapers, and keep a multi-country compliance calendar on track.
* Agency: A high degree of initiative and comfort with ambiguity. You will set your own priorities and build processes where none exist yet.

**Even better if you have**
---------------------------

* Industry: Tax experience at a marketplace, gig, delivery, or AI data company that pays across many countries.
* Emerging markets: Corporate and indirect tax experience in emerging markets, where rules change often and published guidance is thin.
* Transactions: Tax structuring for asset and share acquisitions, intellectual property, or data licensing.
* Credits: Research and development tax credit claims in the United States or Canada.
* Build from scratch: Experience building tax processes, controls, and tooling at a venture-backed company.

If you don't check every box above but believe you can do the job, we encourage you to apply — we're looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, we will partner with you to meet your needs.

We may use AI-assisted tools to help evaluate applications against the requirements of this role. These tools support our recruiting team in identifying qualified candidates but do not replace human judgment or limit which applications may be reviewed or considered.

WealthBridge Financial Group helps individuals, families, and business owners build, protect, and grow their wealth. We don’t do one-size-fits-all. Every strategy is personalized and forward-thinking, and it’s grounded in innovation, collaboration, and education. We aim to be the advisors clients trust for life, not just for one transaction.

www.wealthbridgefg.com

**The Opportunity**

We’re growing, and we’re looking for driven, entrepreneurial people to join us as **Financial Professionals** in our Long Island offices in Garden City and Melville. You’ll sit across the table from clients, help them map out their financial future, and build a practice that’s truly yours. You’ll have an experienced, collaborative team behind you every step of the way.

**What You’ll Do**

* **Build lasting relationships.** You’ll earn clients’ trust with a consultative, client-first approach that keeps them with you for years.
* **Design custom strategies.** You’ll dig into each client’s goals and create personalized plans covering retirement, investments, insurance, and estate planning.
* **Educate and empower.** You’ll break down complex topics so clients can make confident, informed decisions.
* **Bring in the experts.** You’ll partner with internal specialists, CPAs, and other professionals to deliver holistic solutions.
* **Grow your book.** You’ll expand your client base through networking, referrals, and marketing, with our support behind you.
* **Stay sharp.** You’ll keep up with market trends, new products, and evolving planning strategies so your clients stay ahead.

 **Requirements**

**Who Thrives Here**

* You think like an entrepreneur and want to build something of your own
* People enjoy talking to you, and you’re good at earning trust
* You want a career and a business you own, not just a paycheck
* You set goals and push yourself to hit them without someone looking over your shoulder
* You’re curious about money: how it grows, how it’s protected, and how it changes lives
* Sales, finance, or client-service experience helps, but hunger and coachability matter more

**Who You’ll Help**

Your clients will include:

* **Individuals and families** building security and planning for the future
* **Business owners** protecting what they’ve built and planning their next move
* **Institutions and organizations** that need a trusted financial partner

**Why WealthBridge?**

* **No ceiling.** Your growth is tied to your effort, not to a salary band or a seniority list.
* **Real mentorship.** You’ll learn from experienced leaders who want you to win.
* **A team culture.** We collaborate, share what works, and celebrate each other’s success.
* **Meaningful work.** You’ll help people make some of the biggest financial decisions of their lives with clarity and confidence.
* **A firm built on people.** Impact and outcomes come first, for our clients and for our agents.

  
**Benefits**

**What Sets Us Apart**

* **You’re never on your own.** You’ll work alongside a network of experienced professionals and mentors, and you’ll have consultants through Integrated Wealth Resources to help with complex client cases.
* **Tools that do the heavy lifting.** We provide advanced planning resources, digital marketing support, and business development systems so you can focus on clients.
* **Your career, your way.** The path is flexible and built for entrepreneurs, so you can grow at your own pace and shape what you build.
* **We invest in you from day one.** That includes licensing support, ongoing training, and continued professional development as you advance.
* **Modern technology.** Our platforms streamline client engagement and planning, so you spend less time on paperwork and more time making an impact.
* **Integrity comes first.** Our culture is built on doing right by clients, embracing innovation, and earning trust over the long term.

Hennepin Technical College

Accounting Officer Inter

214: Minnesota Association of Professional Employees

Non Job Exempt

Full time

Classified - Unlimited

$26.89 - $39.22  
  

**Job Description**

The position is responsible for managing reconciliation processes for all College-wide revenue resources and disbursements recorded in the State of Minnesota’s Statewide Integrated Financial Tools (SWIFT) and Minnesota State accounting and procurement systems, including Workday and ISRS. The position also performs accounting functions associated with the College’s local banking operations and maintains relationships with the College’s local bank.

  

The position maintains large state-federal and state-county fiscal accounts in compliance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), as well as federal, state, and Minnesota State policies and regulations. Responsibilities include preparing complex financial reports to meet institutional and departmental needs and objectives; assisting in the development and implementation of procedures and policies related to assigned functions; and performing highly technical reconciliation activities requiring extensive knowledge of accounting principles and banking practices.

  

The position is responsible for a variety of accounting-related functions that must be performed accurately and in a timely manner in accordance with GAAP and applicable federal, state, and Minnesota State policies and regulations. The position also serves as the primary contact with the credit card processing company used by the College and coordinates related activities to ensure accurate and efficient processing of credit card transactions.

  

**Salary Range:**

$26.89 - $39.22 Hourly

  

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Minimum of three years of relevant experience in accounting.\*
* Experience reconciling general ledger accounts in a complex accounting system and cash flow monitoring with knowledge of banking practices.
* Knowledge and experiencing applying GAAP accounting principles.
* Ability and experience preparing complex financial reports, locate errors, and recommend solutions.

* Analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail and accuracy.

* Ability to maintain confidentiality of sensitive financial information.

* Knowledge of budgeting principles sufficient to prepare, analyze, monitor and review department budgets.
* Advanced knowledge and skill applying Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.) and Adobe Acrobat, and other financial systems and reporting tools.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills to be able to prepare and present financial reports.

* A Bachelor's degree in a related field may substitute for 12 months of experience and an Associate's degree may substitute for 6 months.

  

**Preferred Qualification**

* Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
* Experience working with auditors.
* Experience and knowledge of process improvement concepts.
* Experience working in a higher education environment.
Customer service skills and interpersonal relationship skills to be able to work with employees at all levels in the College.  

**Other Requirements**

Hennepin Technical College is currently unable to sponsor work visas or green card applications due to regulatory complexity, budget constraints, and alignment with our current hiring strategy. Applicant must be legally authorized to work in the US at the start of employment.

  

**Work Shift (Hours / Days of work)**

M-F / Dayshift

  

**Telework (Yes/No)**

Yes - Hybrid (1 day a week)

  

**About**

Founded in 1972, Hennepin Technical College is the largest technical college in Minnesota. With campuses in Brooklyn Park and Eden Prairie, Hennepin Technical College has a diverse student population of more than 9,500 and offers degree and non-degree coursework in over 45 programs. Achieving a 99% job placement rate within its network of industry partners, Hennepin Technical College prepares students for in-demand and high-paying employment opportunities Hennepin Technical College is a member of Minnesota State, which includes 30 community and technical colleges and seven state universities serving approximately 400,000 students. It is the fourth-largest system of two-year colleges and four-year universities in the United States.

Hennepin Technical College with campuses in Brooklyn Park and Eden Prairie is a member of the Minnesota State Colleges and Universities System. The college is strategically positioned to meet the economic and workforce development needs of business and industry throughout Minnesota. Hennepin Technical College faculty and staff are committed to preparing students to be successful in obtaining the education and skills that can result in employment and a career. Curriculum is industry validated and delivered in an environment that emulates the work setting. Students receive a well-rounded educational experience that gives them the skills and ability to secure the first job in their career as well as to advance in their career. For more information about Hennepin Technical College, please visit our website at: http://www.hennepintech.edu

Revenue Engineering builds the platform that measures how customers use Datadog and turns that measurement into usage and cost data they can act on. Every product Datadog ships is metered here. As a **Staff Product Manager** for **Metering and Cost Attribution**, you will own product direction for that platform. You will set the standard for how usage is measured, attributed, and presented across Datadog.

The role starts with tagging: the mechanism customers use to attribute usage to owners inside their organization, and the foundation that cost allocation, chargeback, quotas, and governance build on. From there you will shape the metering capabilities that new pricing and packaging models draw on, and extend the platform's speed and scale as Datadog's portfolio grows. Over time you will own the vision and roadmap for a usage platform used by every team at Datadog and relied on by every customer.

The usage layer is the system of record for consumption, and it is what billing draws from. What you own is the path from usage events to billable output, along with the consumption models, cost attribution, and usage analytics that customers and their finance teams use to understand their spend. You will partner closely with the billing platform team across that boundary.

Usage and cost attribution reach across a broad portfolio of billable metrics, several regions, and customers organized into parent and child organizations and reseller hierarchies, and they surface in units and in dollars, in-app, through the API, and in agentic workflows. Designing for that range means making deliberate choices about granularity, timeliness, and flexibility, and holding those choices steady across the many teams that build on them.

This is a highly visible individual contributor role spanning several engineering teams, every product vertical that emits billable telemetry, and partners in Sales, Support, and Finance.

### **What You'll Do:**

* **Set product direction for metering and attribution** by defining the problems and outcomes that matter from usage events through billable output, holding a multi-quarter view of how the platform should evolve, and collaborating with multiple engineering teams to sequence work into phases that deliver clear customer value along the way.
* **Own the tagging model as a customer-facing product**, giving customers a consistent way to define tags across every product, translating those tags into granular usage and cost breakdowns wherever they surface, and designing how customers adjust and reconstruct attribution when their tagging changes.
* **Define the metering and rating capabilities that pricing and packaging depend on**, working ahead of launches on usage aggregation, unit definitions, commitments, included usage, and overage, so that the metering platform stays ahead of Datadog's commercial needs.
* **Act as the subject matter expert for metering and cost attribution across Datadog**, setting the standard that product verticals build against when they bring a new SKU into usage attribution, aligning engineering, Cloud Cost Management, Support, Sales, and Finance on a single cost allocation model, and mentoring product managers taking on metering work in their own areas.
* **Own the quality standard for usage data**, translating what customers need in accuracy, timeliness, and auditability into product requirements and service objectives, keeping measured usage, attribution, and billing consistent with one another, and producing the sizing and impact analysis that engineering leadership and pricing partners need to resource the work.

 - Deal desk: Build and run one front door for pricing across our sales, partnerships, capture, and data acquisition teams, with a standard intake, approval thresholds, and an answer within an agreed turnaround.  - Deal performance: Track every signed deal against its model, report actual margin and cash by customer and partner, and feed what you learn back into pricing and the forecast.

 - Agency: A high degree of initiative and comfort with ambiguity. You will set your own priorities and build processes where none exist yet.

 - Industry: Strategic finance or pricing at a two-sided marketplace, delivery, gig, or AI data company, where both supply and demand are priced.

 Blue Rose Research is hiring a Policy Fellow to help design an economic plan for the AI era: a concrete policy agenda for how the country should respond as AI changes jobs, wages, and the economy. The Policy Lead will own the policy substance of the plan. They will identify its key choice points, such as how to support workers whose jobs change, how to share the gains from AI, and how to pay for it, develop realistic options for each, and work through those trade-offs with our research team.
 Reporting to the Director of External Affairs, the Policy Lead will work closely with our data scientists and survey researchers.  Policy Design 
- Lead development of the AI economic plan, from first framework to final proposals
- Identify the plan's key choice points and lay out clear, realistic options for each, including trade-offs, costs, and precedents
- Draw on existing research and proposals on automation, labor markets, the social safety net, workforce training, tax policy, and competition
- Draft policy memos, option papers, and the plan itself
 Working with the Research Team 
- Turn policy options into concrete proposals our research team can test with voters through polling and message testing
- Work through the plan's choice points with the research team, and use results to refine the plan based on what is popular, what is persuasive, and what is sound policy
- Make sure our survey questions describe policies accurately and compare alternatives fairly, including their costs, eligibility, and timing
 Expert & Government Engagement 
- Consult economists, policy experts, former officials, and current federal and state policymakers to pressure-test ideas

- Brief Blue Rose leadership and partners on the plan, its choice points, and the evidence behind our recommendations
 About You 
- Policy Expertise: Deep knowledge of economic policy, such as labor, social insurance, tax, industrial, or technology policy
- Experience: Typically 7+ years of policy experience, including time in the federal executive branch, Congress, a governor's office, or state government
- Policy Builder: You have taken a policy from an idea to a detailed proposal and know the decisions that have to be made along the way
- Structured Thinker: You can break a big question into clear decisions with defined options and trade-offs
- Comfortable with Data: Interested in public opinion research and comfortable working alongside data scientists. You do not need to be a statistician.
- Communication Skills: An exceptional writer who can explain complex economic policy to political and general audiences
- Pragmatic: You care about policy that works and can also pass
- Collaborative: You work well across disciplines and welcome having your ideas tested against evidence
 Bonus Points 
- White House or federal agency experience, such as at the National Economic Council, Domestic Policy Council, Council of Economic Advisers, or Office of Science and Technology Policy
- Relationships with California policymakers or in California's tech and policy community
- Familiarity with research on AI's economic effects, including automation, labor displacement, and productivity
- Experience with polling, message testing, or survey research
- Experience at a think tank or policy research organization
 What We Offer

- Impact: You will shape a concrete plan for how the country handles one of the biggest economic shifts in generations, grounded in what the public actually wants
 About Blue Rose Research 
 Blue Rose Research builds data and AI tools that help Democrats win elections. Our team combines engineering, data science, and political strategy to power decisions for the country's top campaigns and progressive organizations. We forecast elections, test ads, and use generative AI to help campaigns understand what's happening in the news and respond fast with messages that actually work. We have guided how hundreds of millions of dollars are spent in modern campaigns. We're a small, mission-driven team that builds fast, experiments boldly, and helps progressives communicate and win—guided by curiosity, purpose, and a genuine desire to use technology for good.

 At PGIM, You Can!

 The PGIM Strategy team supports the CEO of PGIM and the whole leadership team in developing and executing strategy around the business’ most critical priorities. - Lead competitor intelligence, industry benchmarking, and thematic research initiatives covering traditional and alternative asset management.

- Entrepreneurial spirit and ability to work independently
- Interest in business strategy/development and asset management

Job Description:
 The Macro and Credit Research team evaluates and recommends investment strategies for internal and external clients. Its coverage spans fixed income, credit, and macro strategies, including long-only and hedge fund approaches.  
 The Senior Research Analyst conducts in-depth research on third-party investment managers and their strategies. Working with senior members of the team, the analyst builds manager relationships, gathers and evaluates investment and operational information, applies quantitative tools, and identifies the key drivers of strategy performance, risk, and fit.  
 The role is expected to take ownership of defined manager research assignments, develop well-supported views and ranking recommendations, and contribute investment ideas for client and Russell portfolios. The analyst will also help strengthen research processes and produce clear, decision-useful analysis for investment teams and clients.  
 The successful candidate brings strong fixed-income knowledge, sound investment judgment, and experience analyzing portfolios using both qualitative and quantitative methods. Experience researching external investment managers is required as is knowledge of the fixed income manager universe . Strong communication and relationship-management skills are essential, as the role involves regular interaction with investment managers, colleagues, and clients. Programming skills, particularly in Python, are important; experience with VBA, SQL, or other analytical tools is also valuable.

- Collect, organize, and validate data to support manager and strategy research.  
- Conduct detailed quantitative and qualitative analysis of investment managers and their strategies.  
- Develop and maintain working relationships with third-party investment managers.

 The Sort Capacity Manager owns network-wide capacity de-risking for the Sort organization. This role builds and maintains the constraint model that defines what “de-risked capacity” means across every 1P and 3P facility — dock door availability, floor/pallet-position space, max throughput, and optimal labor and automation. 
 About the Team 
- Own the network constraint model — Model site capacity against its underlying constraints: dock door availability (inbound/outbound truck cadence by hour, translated from Mx forecast), floor/pallet-position space (inbound-to-outbound hourly volume vs. staging capacity), max throughput (automation vs. manual sortation rate, package profile mix, cross-dock vs. sort), and optimal labor hours required to hit max output.
- Govern spoke capacity data — Drive spoke capacity maintenance in the sort app, ensuring product reflects current facility configuration, and hold cross-functional partners accountable when it doesn't.
- Own zip-to-facility strategy — Own zip code-to-facility mapping and re-optimization as volume and rates shift, balancing service-level and cost trade-offs.
- Own device and consumable readiness — Forecast scanners, bins, and gaylords against site growth to avoid reactive procurement; own the readiness cadence end to end.
- Scope hub-to-spoke routing opportunities — Build the business case for hub-sort-to-spoke direct routing and bring recommendations forward to Network Design and Real Estate.
- Close forecasting product gaps — Identify where forecasting tools fail to capture capacity reality and drive the fix with Data/Product partners.
- Own Mx launch — Own Mx launch end to end, including CET allocation by merchant priority, negotiating trade-offs across competing merchant demands.
 You're excited about this opportunity because you will… 
- 3-6-12 month runway visibility ahead of any projected capacity constraint.
- Site launch recommendations delivered proactively, not reactively.
- % of high-priority Mx launches assigned an optimal CET.

- Strategic model ownership — You've built and owned a capacity, forecasting, or network constraint model that became a standing input to planning — not a one-off analysis.
- Independent judgment — You can independently judge where the real bottleneck is across a large, multi-site network, without a pre-scoped problem statement.
- Cross-functional negotiation — You've negotiated trade-off recommendations with senior, cross-functional stakeholders (e.g., Network Design, Real Estate, Finance) and influenced capital-adjacent decisions.
- Physical operations fluency — You understand physical warehouse operations deeply enough to translate dock, floor, throughput, and labor constraints into a single model.
- Experience — 7+ years in supply chain, network strategy, or operations, with direct experience owning capacity planning or site launch strategy at scale.

location: New York, New York; Chicago, Illinois; Boston, Massachusetts; San Francisco Bay Area; Remote
description:
Why We Exist

Your car and your home are your most important assets, yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every part of the journey — buy/sell, insurance, maintenance, repairs — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

 

Jerry.ai http://Jerry.ai is building the first app to manage it all. We started with car insurance in 2019, became one of the top 3 brokers in the U.S., then added driving insights, diagnostics, and a repair marketplace. 

 

We've reached 5M+ customers, raised $240M+, scaled revenue 70X, and became profitable in early 2024. We're now expanding into adjacent verticals (e.g. home, motorcycle, RV, etc) to become the one-stop-shop for all your physical assets.

 

Why We’re Hiring

Our Business Operations & Analytics  team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

 

Every business unit has a Business Operations & Analytics team member embedded within it  —  someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years. 

 

As our business continues to expand, there is growing demand for more Business Operations & Analytics team members. We are hiring 2-3 people to drive impact in these areas:

 - Growth Marketing 

 - Product Development

 - AI & Automation

 - Strategic Partnerships 

 

On leveling: You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.

 

Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

 - No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc. 

 - No corporate fluff: The Business Operations & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals. 

 - Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end. 

 

What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central Business Operations & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

 - Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.

 - Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.

 - Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.

 

Who You Are

 - First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?" 

 - Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.

 - Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

 

What You'll Bring

 - 1+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.

 - Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.

 - Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.

 - Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

 

Our Tools

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

 
 

While we appreciate your interest and application, due to the volume of applications we receive, only applicants under consideration will be contacted.

We are dedicated to ensuring that Braze's financial health is not only robust but also constantly evolving. Our pursuit is to provide a financial foundation that enables the company to thrive and adapt in a dynamic business landscape.
 WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Collaborate with internal and external auditors to provide necessary documentation and support during audits
- Support daily cash management activities, including cash positioning, forecasting, and reporting
- Assist in the preparation and processing of wire transfers, ACH payments, and other cash disbursements
- Assist in maintaining and monitoring relationships with banking partners
- Support the opening, closing, and maintenance of bank accounts and associated services
- Help manage bank fee analysis and optimize banking services
- Assist in the implementation of the new Treasury Management System, including data migration, system configuration, testing, training, and user documentation
- Support overall bank portal and TMS maintenance, along with associated controls
- Help manage inter-company funding and settlement processes
- Provide analytical support for various treasury projects and initiatives
- Maintain accurate and organized records of all treasury transactions and activities
- Ensure compliance with company policies and procedures related to treasury operations
 WHO YOU ARE 
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field
- 1+ years of experience in treasury, finance, or accounting roles
- Basic understanding of SOX compliance and internal controls
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel
- Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills
- Strong written and verbal English language skills are essential
 Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience with treasury management systems and bank portals
- Knowledge of cash management and banking practices
- Previous experience in system implementation projects is a plus

Job Description Summary 
You will lead the enterprise people and organization agenda for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI) across Novartis, translating our DSAI ambition into the workforce, organization, talent and capability choices needed to deliver it. Operating at the decision-making table with senior DSAI leaders and partnering across the enterprise, you will shape how we build, attract and grow critical DSAI talent, strengthen our external value proposition, and enable responsible human-AI collaboration. You will lead the enterprise DSAI OTR, including discussion at ECN level, and create the standards, governance and frameworks needed in areas such as careers, capabilities, talent and rewards, particularly where established approaches do not yet exist.
This enterprise role complements rather than replaces the Workforce Strategy Leads directly supporting DSAI teams within their units. Unit-level accountabilities remain unchanged, while this role connects across them, providing the overarching DSAI people strategy, standards and governance and enabling enterprise-level choices where these are needed.

 This role can be based in Cambridge, East Hanover, London or Basel, please only apply to one of the appropriate location.
 Key Responsibilities 
- Set the enterprise DSAI people and organization strategy.
Translate the DSAI ambition into an integrated, future-ready agenda across workforce, organization, leadership, culture, talent and capability. Success is evident when: enterprise priorities and accountabilities are clear, adopted across units, and translated into measurable outcomes. 
- Shape strategic workforce and capability choices. Use scenarios, analytics, external insight and data storytelling to anticipate demand for scarce DSAI capabilities and recommend choices on organization design, skills, capacity, location, sourcing and workforce mix. Success is evident when: critical gaps are addressed before they constrain innovation or execution. 
- Lead the enterprise DSAI OTR. Orchestrate the enterprise talent review, integrate perspectives across units, and present implications, choices and recommendations to ECN. Success is evident when: pivotal talent, succession, capability risks and enterprise actions are visible and actively managed. 
- Establish enterprise talent and career approaches. Create differentiated career development, mobility, succession and talent-allocation mechanisms suited to DSAI roles and communities. Success is evident when: Novartis can attract, develop, deploy and retain pivotal DSAI talent across organizational boundaries. 
- Build the external DSAI talent brand and pipeline. Strengthen Novartis’ visibility as an employer of choice through targeted engagement with universities, specialist talent networks and external forums. Build early-talent pathways that attract dual technical/scientific and DSAI expertise and develop judgement, experience and leadership capability. Success is evident when: Novartis has stronger external visibility and a sustainable pipeline of scarce DSAI talent. 
- Design and create enterprise DSAI standards. Build new governance, rewards approaches, career architecture, capability frameworks, talent programs and operating approaches for a field evolving faster than established internal practices. Success is evident when: scalable standards replace fragmented local approaches and remain relevant as DSAI evolves. 
- Connect enterprise strategy and unit execution. Define decision rights, interfaces and governance so the enterprise mandate is distinct from, and complementary to, unchanged unit-level P&O accountabilities. Success is evident when: there is no duplication or accountability gap between enterprise and unit roles. 
- Influence a complex enterprise stakeholder system. Partner with at least nine ECN-1 leaders across R&D, Commercial, Operations and Global Functions, the Head of GDC, unit P&O Business Partners and Expertise Hubs to resolve enterprise trade-offs without relying on formal authority. Success is evident when: leaders move beyond unit optimization and commit to enterprise decisions. 
- Redesign work for human-AI collaboration. Guide organization, role and workflow choices that enable responsible collaboration among people, automation and AI agents while sustaining accountability and a human-cantered employee experience. Success is evident when: adoption improves productivity, innovation and decision quality. 
- Coach senior leaders, shape culture and lead transformation. Challenge and coach leaders through ambiguity, build commitment to new enterprise approaches, anticipate resistance and track adoption and benefits. Success is evident when: leadership behaviour, culture and ways of working support the DSAI strategy. 
 What you’ll bring to the role
 Essential Criteria 
- Extensive experience of progressive P&O/HR experience, including strategic partnership with executive and ECN-1 leaders in a complex global matrix. 
- Strong organization design, strategic workforce planning and transformation experience, including scenario development and enterprise trade-off recommendations. 
- Demonstrated experience creating global or enterprise-wide people strategies, standards, governance or programs, not only implementing established solutions. 
- Evidence of leading enterprise talent reviews, succession and capability discussions with senior executive forums. 
- Demonstrated ability to influence multiple senior stakeholders across business units, functions, countries and P&O disciplines without formal authority. 
- Fluency in people analytics and confidence with AI-enabled tools, responsible AI principles and emerging work technologies. 
 Desirable Criteria 
- Experience translating emerging technology, data science or digital strategy into workforce, organization and talent implications; direct DSAI sector experience is highly desirable. 
- Relevant university degree or equivalent exp

 The BlackRock Transformation Office (BTO) is a global group of change professionals that delivers strategic transformation to help make BlackRock greater than the sum of its parts. We drive 1BLK outcomes by continuously connecting and being students of the firm’s people, processes and technology.

- Proficiency in prototype-led problem solving and rapidly converting ambiguous business problems into functional prototypes that stakeholders can see, test and challenge.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.  

 

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.



 


THE ROLE

We are looking for Android software engineers to build the native Android experience for Doit's AI Finance Agent.

This role is for someone who cares about clean user flows, fast performance, product quality and shipping reliable mobile features used by real customers.

 


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Build and ship Android features using Kotlin.

 - Create clean mobile flows for insurance, payments, claims, renewals and financial services.

 - Work with product and design to simplify complex user journeys.

 - Integrate backend APIs and ensure mobile flows are stable, secure and reliable.

 - Improve app performance, crash rate, loading states, responsiveness and memory usage.

 - Use analytics, user behaviour and production issues to improve the product.

 - Build AI-assisted mobile experiences only where they genuinely improve the user journey.

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years of Android development experience using Kotlin.

 - Strong Android fundamentals and experience shipping production apps.

 - Good knowledge of Jetpack, Coroutines, Flow and modern Android architecture.

 - Strong sense of mobile UX, usability, edge cases and user flows.

 - Experience integrating REST APIs and debugging production issues.

 - Fast execution, high ownership and strong attention to product quality.

 - App links, GitHub, screenshots or examples of shipped work are a strong advantage.

 


TECH STACK

 - Kotlin

 - Jetpack Compose

 - Android SDK

 - Coroutines & Flow

 - SQL / NoSQL

 - TensorFlow Lite (on-device inference)

 


THE KIND OF BUILDER WE WANT

 - Thinks in user journeys, not just screens.

 - Cares about making complex financial products feel simple.

 - Moves fast without creating messy code.

 - Notices UX, performance and reliability issues before users complain.

 - Honest about what they personally built, what was team-owned and what impact they can or cannot claim.

 


THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR

 - Engineers who only want fully defined tickets.

 - Developers who build screens without caring about user experience.

 - People who ignore crashes, edge cases, loading states or performance.

 - Engineers who move slowly in a startup environment.

 - People who exaggerate impact without explaining their actual contribution.

 


LOCATION

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in US. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in US.

 


LANGUAGE

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

 


INTERVIEW PROCESS

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round

Jerry is expanding into several new markets at the same time. Capital allocation is now one of the most consequential decisions we make: each dollar committed to a new product line, a marketing channel, or a headcount is a dollar not available elsewhere.

The operating core is the model, the planning cadence, and the spend discipline the company runs on.  - Build the financial model for new product, vertical, channel or partnership: Size the market, model the economics, evaluate capital commitment and return profile.

 - Hands-on fluency with AI tools for analysis, research, and workflow automation.

You’ll report directly to our Founder and work closely with leaders across the company as we scale.

description:
Why Thunderbird? 
 Thunderbird is one of the world’s most trusted open-source email applications, empowering more than 20 million people globally. At Thunderbird, we build privacy-respecting communication and productivity tools that help people manage their digital lives while staying in control of their data. 
 We are open source by design. Our products are developed transparently and in collaboration with a global community of contributors, and that same spirit shapes how we work: collaboratively, inclusively, and with a shared commitment to putting users first. 
 We are a small but growing company of 70+ people distributed across seven countries. As Thunderbird evolves beyond a single desktop application, we are expanding across desktop, mobile, paid services, and new product experiences that help people and organizations work more effectively without giving up control to big tech ecosystems. 
 Our revenue model combines user donations, which help keep Thunderbird’s apps freely available, with paid services that cover the costs of hosted offerings while supporting long-term sustainability and continued innovation. 
 A note about Thunderbird and Mozilla: Thunderbird Technologies Corporation is the nonprofit-owned company behind Thunderbird email and a growing portfolio of products. While part of the Mozilla family, Thunderbird is a separate entity from Mozilla Corporation and Mozilla Foundation with its own compensation programs, benefits, and employment policies .
 To learn more, visit www.thunderbird.net 
 The opportunity 
 We are looking for a Senior Manager, Accounting & Finance to serve as Thunderbird’s most senior finance professional. The right person will bring a strong accounting or controllership foundation and the breadth to lead financial planning and analysis, finance operations, and organization-level decision support. 
 As Thunderbird grows across donations, subscription services, enterprise offerings, and international operations, our financial needs are becoming more complex. We need stronger integration across accounting and FP&A, experienced oversight of emerging revenue models and tax obligations, and clear financial analysis that helps leadership understand performance, risks, tradeoffs, and decisions. 
 Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Head of Finance will directly manage our Senior Staff Accountant and Senior FP&A Analyst. This is a hands-on functional leadership role for someone who can provide experienced financial judgment, develop an established team, and remain close to the details while helping build the systems, controls, reporting, and finance practices the organization needs for its next stage of growth. 
 This role requires regular working-hour overlap with the COO, finance team, and other colleagues across North American time zones. Candidates based in Eastern or Central time zones are preferred; candidates elsewhere in the United States should be comfortable maintaining substantial overlap with those working hours. Flexibility for meetings with colleagues, advisers, and affiliated organizations in Europe is also expected. 
 What you’ll do  
- Lead Thunderbird’s finance function, with overall responsibility for accounting, financial planning and analysis, tax, treasury, and finance operations . 
- Manage and develop Thunderbird’s finance team , establishing clear priorities, responsibilities, review practices, and accountability . 
- Oversee monthly and annual close, financial reporting, reconciliations, accounting policies, and internal controls. 
- Oversee accounting and revenue recognition across donations, subscriptions, enterprise arrangements, partnerships, and other revenue streams. 
- Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, longer-range financial planning, and scenario analysis. 
- Develop clear management reporting and visualizations that highlight important trends, risks, tradeoffs, and decisions. 
- Oversee tax, audit, indirect tax, VAT/GST, corporate filings , and related work with external advisers. 
- Evaluate the financial, tax, accounting, and operational implications of entering new jurisdictions or establishing additional entities . 
- Work with Enterprise Partnerships and Legal to establish financial reporting, reconciliation, and control processes for partner-led commercial arrangements . 
- Oversee financial reporting to Thunderbird’s parent organization and affiliated Mozilla organizations. 
- Own financial oversight of payroll across multiple providers in partnership with the People team. 
- Document and strengthen finance systems and workflows, including accounting, expense management, payment-platform reconciliation, documentation, and automation. 
- Oversee cash-flow planning, treasury, banking, and investment activities, working closely with the Senior FP&A Analyst. 
- Serve as a trusted finance adviser to organizational leaders, translating complex financial information into clear recommendations . 
 What you bring  
- 15+ years of relevant professional experience, including progressively responsible roles spanning accounting, financial planning and analysis, and finance operations. 
- Significant accounting or controllership experience, including responsibility for U.S. GAAP financial reporting, close processes, internal controls, revenue recognition, and complex accounting judgments. 
- 5+ years of people management experience in a finance or accounting environment, including coaching, feedback, prioritization, performance support, career development, and team development. 
- Demonstrated ability to improve budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, and financial data visualization and translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations for non-finance leaders. 
- Substantive experience with subscription, SaaS, digital-product, enterprise, or comparable technology-based revenue models. 
- Experience supporting partner-led commercial arrangements, such as reseller, licensing, wholesale, or reve

 Figure Technology Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: FIGR; OPEN: FGRS) is the leading blockchain-native capital marketplace for the origination, funding, sale and trading of tokenized assets. More than 480 partners use its loan origination system and capital marketplace. Collectively, Figure and its partners have originated over $30 billion of loans to date, among other products. The fastest growing components are Figure Connect, its credit marketplace, and Democratized Prime, Figure’s on-chain lend-borrow marketplace. Figure’s ecosystem also includes DART (Digital Asset Registry Technology) for asset custody and lien perfection, and $YLDS, a yield-bearing stablecoin registered with the SEC as a security under the Securities Act of 1933.
Figure is the market leader in real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. The company has received triple-A ratings ratings from S&P and Moody’s on multiple loan securitizations, the first of its kind for blockchain finance.
We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Top 50 Fintech Companies and CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies . 
 About the Role 
 Figure is hiring a Senior Financial Portfolio Analyst – Servicing to provide advanced financial analysis, portfolio performance monitoring, servicing cost modeling, compliance oversight, and forecasting for a servicing portfolio. This role supports cross-functional teams such as Servicing Operations, Capital Markets, Collections/Default, Investor Reporting, and Asset Management.
 What You’ll Do 
- Servicing P&L Management — Maintain and enhance servicing profit-and-loss models, including revenue streams, ancillary fees, sub-servicing costs, advances, late fees, recoveries, and corporate allocations.
- MSR Valuation Support — Support mortgage servicing rights (MSR) valuation by modeling discount rates, CPR/prepayment speeds, delinquency curves, and cost-to-service assumptions.
- Portfolio Analytics — Build dashboards tracking static pool performance, delinquency migration, modification outcomes, foreclosure metrics, and collection effectiveness.
- Revenue & Cost Forecasting — Forecast servicing revenue based on portfolio balance, runoff, payoffs, and interest-rate conditions; develop models for default expenses, foreclosure timelines, claim recoveries, and REO performance.
- Risk & Compliance Monitoring — Provide financial performance analysis, risk assessment, and compliance monitoring for servicing portfolios.
- Escrow & Advance Modeling — Model escrow balances, interest earnings, advance recoverability, and servicing cost allocations by investor.
- Operational & Strategic Support — Contribute financial insights to operational efficiency initiatives.
- Reporting & Executive Presentations — Prepare monthly business review decks, variance analysis, margin analytics, and operational KPIs for senior leadership.
 What We Look For 
  Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Statistics, Business, or related field.
- 4–7 years of mortgage FP&A, servicing analytics, or portfolio-analysis experience.
- Strong understanding of MSR economics , delinquency modeling, advance mechanics, and servicing cost structures.
- Experience with servicing systems such as MSP, Sagent, LoanServ , and data analysis tools such as SQL, Snowflake, Tableau, Power BI .
- Ability to work independently and manage complex workloads with strict deadlines.
   Preferred Qualifications 
- Master’s degree (MBA or related).
- CPA or similar financial certification (preferred).

- Quarterly 25% bonus target

 iCapital is seeking a skilled and dynamic Associate to join our Revenue Control team within the Corporate Finance organization.  Responsibilities 
- Perform revenue calculations and controls for various product lines across iCapital, primarily Technology Solutions.
- Ensure precision in monthly and quarterly revenue estimates and actuals, providing insightful analyses of variances.
- Foster a culture of financial excellence by collaborating with client relationship managers, finance leadership and external client contacts.
- Review legal agreements, contracts and other key documents and understand relevant economic terms as they relate to revenue and reporting and apply that understanding to revenue calculations.
- Support full revenue cycle including order processing, invoicing, payment collection and revenue recognition, ensuring accuracy and efficiency.
- Spearhead month-end close processes, preparing revenue calculations and revenue accruals for technology solutions products.
- Calculate and consolidate P&L and balance sheet data, ensuring accurate journal entries for various entities.
- Assist with the calculation and generation of invoices at month end.
- Perform month over month roll forwards for key revenue metrics.
- Prepare detailed monthly revenue reconciliation analyses supporting accurate P&L reporting.
- Execute cash application processes and prepare monthly cash reconciliations.
- Support the initiative to enhance efficiency and automation of our existing revenue calculations and invoicing processes, including implementation of a new order-to-cash billing and receivable software.
- Develop insightful reporting and analyses to support business unit and product line leads with actionable insights for performance reporting to management and investors.
- Identify and address process gaps, implement robust internal controls, and improve documentation for internal control processes.
- Identify opportunities to streamline processes by leveraging automation tools and data-driven workflows to improve efficiency and accelerate task completion.
 Qualifications 
- 2-5 years of corporate accounting or public accounting experience within the financial services industry
- Outstanding financial analysis skills and knowledge of accounting principles and US GAAP reporting
- Strong ability to apply critical thinking skills to analyze complex issues and propose effective solutions, while consistently maintaining a meticulous attention to detail
- Organized and detail-oriented process manager who can prioritize and communicate clearly with senior leadership
- Experience with revenue, treasury management, accounts receivable and payable, and cash reconciliations
- Knowledge of booking journal entries and preparation of financial statements
- Data-driven thinker who can manage large data sets for efficient analyses
- Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills
- Able to coordinate across teams and departments to complete projects
- CPA license is preferred but not required
- Degree in Accounting is preferred but not required
- Familiar with Oracle NetSuite or other general ledger systems (i.e. Quickbooks) is preferred
- Familiar with alternative investments or structured investments is preferred
 Benefits 
 The base salary range for this role is $85,000 to $110,000.  iCapital offers a compensation package which includes salary, equity for all full-time employees, and an annual performance bonus. Employees also receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes an employer matched retirement plan, generously subsidized healthcare with 100% employer paid dental, vision, telemedicine, and virtual mental health counseling, parental leave, and unlimited paid time off (PTO).
 We believe the best ideas and innovation happen when we are together. Employees in this role will work in the office Monday-Thursday, with the flexibility to work remotely on Friday.

 The Role 
 We are looking for an experienced FP&A business partner to support our CTO and Engineering organization, as well as our CCO organization, including Professional Services, Support, Training, and Customer Success. This is a Manager-level individual contributor role spanning R&D investment and the direct and indirect costs of delivering and supporting our products.
 Our approach to FP&A is simple: understand what happened, determine why it matters, and help the business decide what to do next.
 Cloud infrastructure economics is central to this role. We want to go significantly deeper than understanding total infrastructure spend or explaining variances. This person will partner closely with Engineering and Tech/FinOps to develop visibility into how architecture, products, customers, usage patterns, capacity, and technical decisions translate into cost and gross margin, and identify opportunities to improve those economics over time.
 The role will also support productivity and operating-leverage analysis across R&D and the CCO organization, connecting investment and capacity to business outcomes and scalability.
 What You’ll Do 
 Business partnering
 CTO / Engineering / R&D
- Serve as a key finance partner to the CTO and Engineering organization, bringing financial and operational insight to R&D investment, resource allocation, productivity, and decision-making.
- Drive deeper understanding of cloud infrastructure economics, partnering with Engineering and Tech/FinOps to connect product and customer usage, architecture, capacity, and consumption to unit economics and gross margin, and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and scalability.
- Bring a productivity lens to R&D investment, helping leaders understand how resources and capacity are deployed, what outcomes they support, and where operating leverage can improve.
- Develop business cases and scenario analyses that inform investment priorities and technical and operating decisions.
 CCO
- Partner with CCO leadership across Professional Services, Support, Training, and Customer Success.
- Develop a clear understanding of the operational drivers of Services margin, capacity, utilization, staffing mix, and cost to serve.
- Bring a productivity lens across customer-facing teams, connecting resources and capacity to business and customer outcomes.
- Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, scalability, and operating leverage while balancing customer needs.
 FP&A & performance management
- Own the budget, forecast, and performance outlook across the supported organizations, ensuring Finance has a clear and reliable view of results, risks, and opportunities.
- Connect business activity and operational drivers to financial outcomes, including gross margin, cost to serve, and R&D investment.
- Contribute to product P&Ls and product-level profitability views by connecting R&D investment, infrastructure costs, and customer-delivery costs to product economics.
- Bring insights from the business back into the broader FP&A organization, helping inform company-level forecasts, planning, and management reporting.
- Explain performance drivers, assess their implications, and recommend appropriate actions.
- Continuously improve models, data, and processes so more time can be spent on analysis and decision
 What You’ll Bring 
- Demonstrated, hands-on depth in SaaS cloud infrastructure economics, including consumption drivers, unit economics, scalability, and gross-margin implications.
- Approximately 5–8+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, strategic finance, finance analytics, FinOps, or a related field.
- Experience in a $300M–$1B PE-backed or pre-IPO enterprise B2B SaaS company, or a highly comparable environment.
- Experience partnering with Engineering, Technology, Product, or Tech/FinOps leaders.
- Strong understanding of SaaS gross margin and cost-to-serve economics.
- Exceptional financial modeling and analytical skills, including the ability to work through complex or imperfect operational data.
- Ability to independently move from analysis to insight to a clear point of view and recommendation.
- Technical curiosity and enough fluency to engage credibly with Engineering and keep digging beyond the first explanation.
- Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively with senior leaders in an individual contributor capacity.
 Better Together 
 Diversity. Inclusion. They’re more than just words for us. They are the guiding values of how we build our teams, cultivate leaders, and create a culture where people feel connected.
 We take care of our employees so they can take care of our customers. Customers who come from all walks of life just like us. We hire incredible people from diverse backgrounds because when we are different together, we are stronger together.
 About Us 
 BeyondTrust is the global identity security leader protecting Paths to Privilege™. Our identity-centric approach goes beyond securing privileges and access, empowering organizations with the most effective solution to manage the entire identity attack surface and neutralize threats, whether from external attacks or insiders.
 BeyondTrust is leading the charge in transforming identity security to prevent breaches and limit the blast radius of attacks, while creating a superior customer experience and operational efficiencies. We are trusted by 20,000 customers, including 75 of the Fortune 100, and our global ecosystem of partners.
